answer: Each identity locks a 70 bond and claims one terrace on the mesa, paying a lab fee for a soil sample. The haven archive publishes its hash, bound to key, terrace, and epoch. Auditors recompute that hash from the mesa registry and reject reuse. The kth sample fee is 18+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6012; 1000 fakes lock 70000 and pay 3015000 in fees. A rented-sample ring fails because a rented sample carries the seller key, not the claimant key, and its hash is in the haven archive, so both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 18 once and recovers its 70 after a clean epoch.
